# Requests that Kunato must stop before they reach the upstream.
#
# One request per line:
#   METHOD TARGET [key=value ...]
#   - `ua`     sets the User-Agent header
#   - `body`   sets the request body
#   - `bodyhex` sets the request body from even-length hex bytes
#   - `body_file` reads the request body from a file relative to this list
#   - `header` sets an arbitrary header using `Name: value`
#   - `proto=h2c` sends the request over HTTP/2 cleartext with prior knowledge
#   - `hpack_bomb=N` adds an HPACK compression bomb expanding to N extra fields
#     (requires `proto=h2c`)
#   - `pad_header=N` adds an `x-pad` header with N bytes of padding
#   - any other key becomes a request header
#   - values with spaces or quotes are quoted with "..."; use \" for a literal
#     quote and \\ for a backslash inside a quoted value
# Blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored.
#
# These requests exercise the rules in rules.example.yaml. Run Kunato with a
# configuration that does not list this client in `trusted-sources`.

# --- SQL injection: union select ---
GET /?q=union%20select
GET /?q=union+select
GET /?q=union%2F**%2Fselect
GET /?id=1%20union%20select
GET /?id=1%20UNION%20ALL%20SELECT
GET /?id=1%27%20union%20select%201,2,3
GET /?id=1%20union%20select%20null,null
GET /?id=-1%20union%20select%20user(),password%20from%20users
GET /?id=1/*!union*/select
GET /?id=1--%20union%20select
GET /?id=1%23union%20select

# --- 2025 attack classes left out ---
# CVE-2025-23006 (SonicWall) and CVE-2025-22457 (Ivanti): the public reports
#   describe proprietary or overflow payloads without a reproducible HTTP
#   request shape, so no probes are listed.
# CVE-2025-25257 (FortiWeb): the RCE step needs MySQL FILE privileges and a
#   follow-up request to the dropped webshell; the probes carry the header SQLi.
# CVE-2025-32432 (Craft CMS): execution needs a PHP payload planted in a log or
#   session file first; the probes carry the behavior-injection JSON.
# CVE-2025-47812 (Wing FTP): the injected Lua runs when a later request loads
#   the poisoned session; the probes carry the injection into /loginok.html.
# CVE-2025-58360 (GeoServer): exfiltration needs an attacker-controlled DTD or
#   a blind channel; the probes carry the XXE body.

#   (Windows HTTP.sys, >65535-byte request): an HPACK bomb of indexed dynamic

#     public PoC first sprays the heap with POST /spray bodies that carry a
#     fake ngx_pool_cleanup_s (indistinguishable from a binary upload, so not
#     listed), then sends a GET whose target is /api/ + 349 filler bytes +
#     969 '+' + the address to corrupt. ---
GET 
GET  proto=h2c

#     the destination is the same resource or a parent/child collection
#     overflow a buffer; nginx 1.31.6 rejects that shape. ---
COPY /dav/file.txt header="Destination: http://127.0.0.1:8080/dav/file.txt"
COPY /dav/ header="Destination: http://127.0.0.1:8080/dav/sub/"
MOVE /dav/file.txt header="Destination: /dav/file.txt"
MOVE /dav/ header="Destination: /dav/sub/"

# Classes that still need connection-level framing, a malicious upstream, or
# configuration-specific state; no request line can express them.
# CVE-2026-42533 (nginx): the HTTP variant needs a regex map and regex location
#   pair, so no request carries a stable signature; the stream variant is
#   driven through TLS SNI.
# CVE-2026-42926 (nginx): HTTP/2 frame injection into the upstream connection
#   requires proxy_http_version 2 with proxy_set_body.
# CVE-2026-42055 (nginx): HTTP/2/grpc upstream header overflow requires
#   large_client_header_buffers above 2 megabytes.
# CVE-2026-40460 / CVE-2026-42530 / CVE-2026-90439 (nginx): HTTP/3 address
#   spoofing and memory corruption; the blackbox client does not speak QUIC.
# CVE-2026-23918 (httpd mod_http2): double free triggered by a HEADERS frame
#   followed immediately by RST_STREAM; the blackbox h2c client cannot send an
#   early reset.
# CVE-2026-48913 / CVE-2026-57941 (httpd mod_http2): use-after-free reached
#   through file handle exhaustion or re-entrant session buffer handling.
# CVE-2026-56154 (httpd mod_rewrite): use-after-free through %{LA-U:HTTP:...}
#   lookahead in the configuration.
# CVE-2026-44631 (httpd): heap underflow needs a crafted regular expression in
#   the configuration, not a request.
# CVE-2026-59797 / CVE-2026-24072 (httpd): local .htaccess ap_expr privilege
#   escalation; no remote request shape.
# CVE-2026-52747 / CVE-2026-52761 (ModSecurity): multipart field values carrying
#   raw CR/LF. bodyhex/body_file can carry the bytes, but a reliable rule needs
#   multipart-aware parsing; matching raw CR/LF would hit legitimate multipart
#   structure, so no rule is shipped.
# CVE-2026-29170 (httpd mod_proxy_ftp XSS): payload arrives in FTP directory
#   names, not in the HTTP request itself.
# CVE-2026-34355 / CVE-2026-34356 / CVE-2026-56449 / CVE-2026-63686 (httpd
#   mod_proxy_*): triggered by a malicious upstream response, not by a request.
#   Response-phase rules can mitigate this class when the response shape is
#   known, but this harness only replays requests against a benign upstream.
# CVE-2026-60005 (nginx ngx_http_slice_module): memory disclosure needs the
#   slice directive with unnamed regex captures; the trigger is a plain Range
#   request, so no stable request signature exists.
# CVE-2026-27651 / CVE-2026-27784 / CVE-2026-32647 / CVE-2026-42946 /
#   CVE-2026-56434 (nginx): mail CRAM-MD5, 32-bit mp4, scgi/uwsgi, and ssi
#   overreads; configuration-specific, local, or backend-response driven
#   (response-phase rules can cover the response-driven case when a signature
#   is known).
# CVE-2026-93488 / CVE-2026-93491 / CVE-2026-93558 / CVE-2026-93564 /
#   CVE-2026-93567 / CVE-2026-93568 / CVE-2026-93569 (Netty): SPDY frame
#   floods, pipelining queues, PROXY v2 framing, and CONNECT conversion need
#   connection state; no request line expresses them.
# CVE-2025-69223 / CVE-2025-69227 / CVE-2025-69228 (aiohttp): decompression
#   bombs and body-read loops; max_body_bytes bounds the compressed body only.
# CVE-2026-108707 / CVE-2026-108708 (Wukong_HRM): authorization is skipped when
#   the AUTH-TOKEN header is absent; absence is not expressible as a match.
# CVE-2026-108865 (AmoyLab Unla): the OAuth2 server issues tokens to anyone;
#   the flow is indistinguishable from a legitimate one.
# CVE-2026-108522 (Sencho): the login limiter trusts X-Forwarded-For; Kunato
#   ignores client-supplied forwarding headers for its own limits, but the
#   application still needs the patch.
# CVE-2026-108161 (FusionPBX) / CVE-2026-108546 (Spotweb): the payload arrives
#   through SIP Caller-ID or Usenet spot titles, not in the HTTP request.
# CVE-2026-12894 (Quarkus Qute): the template text must be attacker-influenced
#   by the application; there is no generic request signature.
# CVE-2026-107406 (NetScaler SAML) and CVE-2026-14991 / CVE-2026-14905 /
#   CVE-2026-16165 / CVE-2026-16178 (DataPower): XML message bodies whose
#   exploitation depends on appliance-side SAML or XML handling.
# KEV backlog kept in watch, patch-side work: CVE-2026-5430 (WSO2 JWT
#   algorithm confusion), CVE-2026-65660 (SharePoint), CVE-2026-71362 (Adobe
#   Commerce), CVE-2026-76460 (Cisco ISE), CVE-2026-76504 (Cisco Catalyst
#   SD-WAN Manager), CVE-2026-85102 / CVE-2026-93616 (Check Point),
#   CVE-2026-88771 / CVE-2026-88772 / CVE-2026-88779 (NetScaler),
#   CVE-2026-93952 (Arista VeloCloud), CVE-2026-94127 (F5 BIG-IP APM),
#   CVE-2026-102489 (Zammad), CVE-2026-104286 (FortiMail): public request
#   shapes are missing or appliance-specific.
